THE ANCIENT COVENANT RECORD

Volume Two

4QInstruction — Musar leMevin

MUSAR LEMEVIN

Instruction — Part Two

4Q418, 4Q423 — Columns 13 through 26

Social Ethics — Agricultural Law — Eschatological Judgment — Community Conduct

PRIMARY MANUSCRIPT AUTHORITIES

4Q418 — Cave 4, Qumran — Hebrew — Largest witness — Over 220 fragments

4Q423 — Cave 4, Qumran — Hebrew — Agricultural sections — Secondary witness

Continuation of the Musar leMevin wisdom instruction

No Masoretic parallel — No Christian contamination

COMPARATIVE NOTES AT END OF EVERY CHAPTER

DSS · ORIT GE'EZ · MASORETIC VARIANT · CRITICAL NOTE

YHWH / 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and The Creator only — no substitute titles

PART TWO — SOCIAL ETHICS AND ESCHATOLOGICAL WISDOM — 4Q418 AND 4Q423

COLUMN 13 — CONDUCT WITH THOSE IN AUTHORITY — 4Q418 Fragment 55

1 [Do not speak harshly] to the one who rules over you, whether he is your father or your master or the leader of the community. For YHWH has placed him in authority and to resist authority without cause is to resist the ordering of The Creator.

2 But if the one in authority commands you to transgress the covenant of YHWH or to violate the mystery of existence, do not obey. For YHWH is above all rulers and His counsel stands over every human appointment. Obey The Creator above all.

3 Seek wisdom in the counsel of those older than yourself. Do not despise the instruction of the elders because you have been given understanding. For wisdom comes through years as well as through revelation, and both are gifts of YHWH.

4 Do not exalt yourself above your station. Do not claim honour that has not been given to you. Walk in the place appointed for you and let YHWH exalt you in His time. Self-exaltation is the beginning of the fall.

5 Be faithful in small things. The one who is faithful in what is small will be entrusted with what is great. The one who is negligent in small things will lose even what he has. For the accounting of YHWH is precise.

6 Pursue truth in all your speech. Let no falsehood come from your mouth concerning your neighbour, your creditor, your ruler, or your wife. For the one who speaks truth walks in the light of the mystery of existence.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q418 Fragment 55 is among the better-preserved sections of this manuscript. The instruction concerning authority is notable for its qualification: obey rulers except when they contradict YHWH. This is a pre-political doctrine of conscientious resistance embedded in a wisdom text, not a legal code.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Yovelim 21 contains similar instruction to Yaakov concerning proper conduct with those in authority and the primacy of covenant loyalty over human command. The Afro-Asiatic wisdom tradition consistently places divine authority above human authority without requiring rebellion as the first response.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Mishlei 16:18 states that pride comes before destruction. The 4QInstruction framework develops this into a systematic ethics of social position — know your station, serve faithfully within it, do not grasp beyond it. This is more developed than the isolated Masoretic proverbs.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The doctrine of qualified obedience — obey authority except when it contradicts YHWH — is one of the most politically significant ideas in the entire Qumran corpus. It directly contradicts the Roman imperial theology of absolute obedience to the emperor as divine representative. This text, written during the period of Roman expansion into the region, is implicitly anti-imperial in its political theology.

COLUMN 14 — AGRICULTURAL ETHICS AND FIRST FRUITS — 4Q423 Fragment 1

1 When you harvest the grain of your field, remember that the land belongs to YHWH and you are a steward of what He has given. The first of everything belongs to Him. Do not withhold the first fruits from His appointed place.

2 Leave the corner of your field for the poor who have no field. Leave the gleanings of your harvest for the widow and the stranger. For you were once without and YHWH gave to you. Give now from what He has given.

3 Do not use false weights or deceitful measures. The one who deceives in commerce deceives before YHWH who sees the hidden things. Better a small honest measure than a large dishonest one.

4 Rest the land in its appointed year. Do not drain it beyond what it can bear. For the land also follows the mystery of existence — it has its appointed times of rest and its appointed times of fruitfulness. Violate these and the land will fail you.

5 When you lend to the poor do not take interest. For the poor man is your brother and his poverty is not his crime. YHWH will account to you the interest you did not take as righteousness, and He will account the interest you did take as iniquity.

6 Study the appointed seasons of planting and harvest in the mystery of existence. For YHWH has encoded the agricultural calendar in creation itself. The one who plants in the right season and harvests at the right time works with the order of The Creator.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q423 is the agricultural section of 4QInstruction and is the primary witness for these columns. The integration of agricultural ethics with the raz nihyeh framework is unique — the proper conduct of farming is presented as participation in the divine ordering of creation, not merely practical advice.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez Yovelim extensively regulates agricultural practice within the jubilee framework — sabbatical years, first fruits, corners of the field for the poor. The 4QInstruction agricultural ethics operates within the same Afro-Asiatic covenantal framework, confirming that these practices predate the Masoretic and Rabbinic codifications.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Torah contains agricultural regulations in Vayikra 19 and Devarim 24. 4QInstruction embeds these same regulations within a wisdom framework rather than a legal one — the obligation arises from understanding the mystery of existence, not from legal compulsion. This represents a fundamentally different ethical foundation.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The prohibition of interest on loans to the poor is one of the most consistently violated principles in human economic history. 4QInstruction frames it not as a legal technicality but as a covenant obligation flowing from the wisdom of the raz nihyeh. The one who takes interest from the poor does not merely break a rule — he acts against the moral structure of creation itself.

COLUMN 15 — ESCHATOLOGICAL JUDGMENT AND THE RIGHTEOUS POOR — 4Q418 Fragments 69 and 81

1 [YHWH will judge] all flesh in the last days. The accounting will be precise. Nothing will be forgotten. Every deed done in the body will be presented before Him. The secret counsels of every heart will be read aloud.

2 The righteous poor who studied the mystery of existence and walked in it will be exalted. Their poverty will become their honour and their faithfulness will become their reward. YHWH will seat them with the princes of His holy ones.

3 The rich who oppressed the poor and took from the widow and the stranger will be brought down. Their wealth will testify against them. Their comfort in this age will be exchanged for their judgment in the age to come.

4 Therefore do not envy the prosperity of the wicked in this age. Their prosperity is their last reward. When the appointed time arrives they will have nothing left. But your poverty now is the seed of your eternal inheritance.

5 Hold fast to the mystery of existence in the day of your affliction. When poverty presses you and creditors surround you and your household lacks bread — in that hour especially, study the mystery. For it is the anchor that holds when every other thing gives way.

6 The discerning one who understands the mystery of existence does not fear death. For he knows what comes after it. He has read the accounting of The Creator and he knows that the righteous are not abandoned even in the grave.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q418 Fragments 69 and 81 contain some of the most explicit eschatological material in 4QInstruction. Fragment 69 has been noted by scholars including Matthew Goff as central to understanding how 4QInstruction integrates wisdom and apocalypticism — a combination Western scholarship long claimed was impossible.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The vindication of the righteous poor and the judgment of the oppressive rich is a central theme of Chanokh 92-105 in the Orit Ge'ez — the Epistle of Chanokh. The parallel is precise enough to suggest both texts draw on the same ancient Afro-Asiatic theological tradition of divine economic justice.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Tehillim contains numerous laments of the righteous poor and promises of divine vindication. 4QInstruction transforms these from poetic expression into systematic wisdom instruction: the eschatological vindication is not merely hoped for but known through the raz nihyeh and therefore constitutes a foundation for present ethical behaviour.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The statement that the righteous are not abandoned even in the grave is one of the clearest pre-Christian references to post-mortem existence in the entire DSS corpus. It predates and is independent of any Christian theological development. Western scholarship has consistently downplayed this passage to avoid the implication that resurrection hope existed in Jewish theology before and independent of Christianity.
